newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end lower on local rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end lower on local rate concerns.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed 1.54 percent lower amid worries about the trajectory of local interest rates after the Central Bank surprised the markets by leaving monthly rates for May unchanged, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares lost 147 points to close at 9,419 points. Market turnover was 528.2 million reais ($498.3 million).
Late Wednesday, the Central Bank announced its basic interest rate (TBC) would remain unchanged at 1.58 percent.

Although economists saw the move as a positive step by the government to slow deterioration of Brazil's external accounts, traders had expected the Central Bank to keep lowering rates, but at a slower pace. They also noted that the Central Bank's move reinforced the idea the government will take further measures, probably credit restrictions, to have better control over its foreign accounts.

Stocks of the consumer goods sector have been suffering from mounting speculation that the government is about to restrict credit selectively to reduce imports and tame Brazil's current account gap, traders said.
Most analysts believe Brazil will move to curb consumption of durable and semi-durable goods as sales of electronic, automobiles and beverages continue to rise.

Traders also said concerns over domestic interest rates helped players holding short positions in the options market to pressure share prices down, particularly Telebras . The options will settle next Tuesday.
Telebras preferred fell 1.93 percent to close at 116.50 reais.
Soon to be privatized state mining giant Vale do Rio Doce oil firm Petrobras lost 1.92 percent, closing at 204 reais.
The power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, dropped 0.56 percent to 2,621 points, with federal Eletrobras falling 0.21 percent to end at 479 reais.
Analysts said the market is likely to keep losing ground on Friday, also helped by weaker Wall Street stock prices.
